rationale: Build directly on the 9x512 recurrent-tail winner with a new minimal recurrence transplant instead of another small optimizer sweep. The current best replays the last two decoder blocks against the original token-embedding anchor only; this adds zero-init per-channel recurrent-anchor gates that let each repeated tail block borrow from its own first-pass decoder input inside the block residual mix while preserving the exact baseline at initialization. The change is compile-stable, keeps the exact int8+zlib endgame intact, costs only tiny float-kept control tensors, and targets a narrower anchor path than the earlier full carry-gated or fully anchored misses.
title: Learned First-Pass Anchor On Recurrent Tail
